boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named academic work environments at Pearson Library, each with a documented feature or access condition.

cards.title: Study Room 123
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · individual or small-group work
cards.notes: Reserve this 1–6-person room when you need a contained work session; use its PC, dry-erase board, monitor, and HDMI screen sharing.
cards.short_summary: A reservable small-group room with built-in presentation tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 123 holds 1–6 people and is one of Pearson Library's study rooms with a PC, dry-erase board, TV monitor, and HDMI cable.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations | Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff; students have priority. Reserve during library hours and check in at the Circulation Desk with student ID.

cards.title: Study Room 124
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · individual or small-group work
cards.notes: Book this 1–6-person room for focused work or a compact project meeting, then connect a device to the monitor with the provided HDMI cable.
cards.short_summary: A small reservable room set up for shared screens and notes.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 124 holds 1–6 people and is one of Pearson Library's study rooms with a PC, dry-erase board, TV monitor, and HDMI cable.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations | Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff; students have priority. Reservations are normally available in two-hour blocks during library hours.

cards.title: Study Room 125
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · individual or small-group work
cards.notes: Choose this 1–6-person room when a whiteboard and display will help organize a study plan; ask the Circulation Desk for markers or cables.
cards.short_summary: A reservable room pairing a whiteboard with screen-sharing hardware.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 125 holds 1–6 people and is one of Pearson Library's study rooms with a PC, dry-erase board, TV monitor, and HDMI cable.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations | Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff; students have priority. Check in at the Circulation Desk and leave your ID for the booking.

cards.title: Study Room 126
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · individual or small-group work
cards.notes: Reserve this 1–6-person study room for a bounded work block, using its monitor and HDMI cable to review material together on one screen.
cards.short_summary: A compact, reservable study room with display equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 126 holds 1–6 people and is one of Pearson Library's study rooms with a PC, dry-erase board, TV monitor, and HDMI cable.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations | Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff; students have priority. Reserve during regular library hours; longer bookings depend on availability.

cards.title: Conference Room 133
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · group meetings and presentations
cards.notes: Plan a larger project session here for 7–10 people; bring a laptop to share on the flat-screen display and use the dry-erase boards to map tasks.
cards.short_summary: A larger reservable collaboration room with display and whiteboard tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Conference Room 133 holds 7–10 people and has a PC, flat-screen monitor, wireless mouse and keyboard, HDMI, and dry-erase boards.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations | Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff; faculty and staff have priority. Reserve during library hours and check in at the Circulation Desk.

cards.title: Conference Room 139
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · collaborative projects
cards.notes: Use this 5–8-person room for a presentation rehearsal or team review; its screen-sharing setup and dry-erase boards support visible group work.
cards.short_summary: A mid-sized, reservable room designed for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Conference Room 139 holds 5–8 people and has a PC, flat-screen monitor, wireless mouse and keyboard, HDMI, and dry-erase boards.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations | Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff; faculty and staff have priority. Room reservations are available during regular library hours.

cards.title: Computer Lab 130
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · computer-based work
cards.notes: Reserve this lab when your work needs campus software or many desktop stations; it has 24 PCs, an instructor station with projector, and two dry-erase boards.
cards.short_summary: A technology-heavy room for individual or group computer work.
cards.evidence_claim: Pearson Library's computer lab includes 24 PC workstations, an instructor station with projector, two dry-erase boards, internet access, and specialized software.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations | Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff; faculty and staff have priority. Reserve the room during library operating hours.

cards.title: Active Learning Classroom
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · instructor-reserved collaborative classroom
cards.notes: Use this space only with an instructor-led reservation: six movable tables support group configurations, and each table connects personal computers to a monitor.
cards.short_summary: A structured, technology-equipped room for class-based collaborative learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Active Learning Classroom has six movable tables for groups, monitors at each desk, and an instructor station with computer and projector.
cards.source_title: Active Learning Classroom | Cal Lutheran Registrar
cards.access_notes: Located inside Pearson Library and bookable during library hours. An instructor must reserve it; it is locked when not in use, and food or drink is not permitted.

cards.entity_name: Elton and Janice Gallegly Center for Public Service and Civic Engagement
cards.title: Gallegly Center
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · study and collaboration area
cards.notes: Set up a collaborative session in the center's designated study area, then use the setting to focus a project on public service or civic engagement.
cards.short_summary: A library-based study and collaboration area within a civic-engagement center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Elton and Janice Gallegly Center is located in Pearson Library and includes study and collaboration space.
cards.source_title: Location | Gallegly Center at Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Located in Pearson Library. The university describes the center as a hub for nonpartisan thought leadership; confirm library building access requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Darling Collaboration Suite
cards.subtitle: Pearson Library · Writing Center location
cards.notes: Visit the Writing Center in this library suite to work through a draft or writing project; schedule through MyCLU Blackboard or stop by to arrange an appointment.
cards.short_summary: A named library suite that houses Cal Lutheran's Writing Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran identifies the Darling Collaboration Suite in Pearson Library as the location of its Writing Center and states that members of the Cal Lutheran community with a university email may use Writing Center services.
cards.source_title: Syllabus Policies | Academic Affairs at Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Writing Center appointments are scheduled through the Writing Center tool in MyCLU Blackboard, or visitors may stop by the suite to schedule. University email access is stated for services.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten documented public destinations on corridors in the California Lutheran University orbit, each with one concrete reason to go.

cards.title: Gardens of the World — five garden styles
cards.subtitle: Thousand Oaks Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Walk the paths through the English, French, Italian, Japanese, and California Mission garden areas; check the garden’s posted closure notices before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A 4.5-acre cultural garden with five distinct landscape areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Gardens of the World at 2001 Thousand Oaks Boulevard has five gardens and walking paths with plants, flowers, and water features.
cards.source_title: Gardens of the World
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; last admittance is 4:30 p.m. Closed Sunday and Monday, most national holidays, and during inclement weather.

cards.entity_name: Bank of America Performing Arts Center at the Thousand Oaks Civic Arts Plaza
cards.title: Civic Arts Plaza — a performance calendar
cards.subtitle: Thousand Oaks Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Look up the current program before traveling, then choose a ticketed performance or arts event that fits your schedule and budget.
cards.short_summary: A Thousand Oaks Boulevard performing-arts venue supported by TOArts.
cards.evidence_claim: TOArts presents and supports visual and performing arts at the Bank of America Performing Arts Center, located at 2100 Thousand Oaks Boulevard.
cards.source_title: TOArts — Arts Council of the Conejo Valley
cards.access_notes: Event access, start times, and ticket requirements vary by program; consult the presenter’s current listing.

cards.title: Hillcrest Center — gallery and classes
cards.subtitle: Hillcrest Drive corridor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition or class listing, then plan a daytime visit to see the arts facilities and public gallery programming.
cards.short_summary: A city-owned arts center with theater, visual arts, and class activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillcrest Center for the Arts at 403 West Hillcrest Drive provides community theater, performing and fine arts classes, and music and dance performances.
cards.source_title: Hillcrest Center for the Arts — Arts Council of the Conejo Valley
cards.access_notes: Program, gallery, and performance access varies; confirm the applicable listing or box office information before visiting.

cards.title: Conejo Creek North Park — ponds and paths
cards.subtitle: East Janss Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the 0.67-mile walking path to loop past the two ponds and stream, then pause at the designated Healing Garden with appropriate respect.
cards.short_summary: A creekside park with ponds, paths, picnic areas, and a Healing Garden.
cards.evidence_claim: Conejo Creek North Park at 1379 East Janss Road has two ponds connected by a recirculating stream, a 0.67-mile walking path, and the Healing Garden.
cards.source_title: Conejo Creek North Park — Conejo Recreation & Park District
cards.access_notes: Park hours vary seasonally: 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. November–February, 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. March and October, and 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. April–September.

cards.title: Conejo Creek South Park — field-side walk
cards.subtitle: East Janss Road corridor
cards.notes: Take the 0.65-mile recreational walking path around the sports grounds; give permitted teams space and check field conditions before a visit.
cards.short_summary: A 55-acre park with a recreational path, baseball field, and soccer fields.
cards.evidence_claim: Conejo Creek South Park at 1300 East Janss Road includes a 0.65-mile recreational walking path, one baseball field, and 12 soccer fields.
cards.source_title: Conejo Creek South Park — Conejo Recreation & Park District
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; athletic games must finish and field lights be off by 8:30 p.m.

cards.title: Thousand Oaks Community Park — disc golf
cards.subtitle: North Moorpark Road corridor
cards.notes: Bring a disc for the Rabbit Flats Disc Golf Course, which is first-come, first-served; use the posted park rules and share paths courteously.
cards.short_summary: A 35.8-acre community park with a first-come disc golf course.
cards.evidence_claim: Thousand Oaks Community Park at 2525 North Moorpark Road is home to Rabbit Flats Disc Golf Course, available first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Thousand Oaks Community Park — Conejo Recreation & Park District
cards.access_notes: Park open daily 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; outdoor courts and the disc golf course are first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Conejo Community Park — lawn amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Hendrix Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Bring a blanket for a listed Summer Concerts in the Park date, or use the park’s picnic areas and ballfield during regular park access.
cards.short_summary: An oak-filled community park with a sloped lawn amphitheater.
cards.evidence_claim: Conejo Community Park at 1175 Hendrix Avenue has picnic areas, a ballfield, and a sloped-lawn amphitheater that hosts Summer Concerts in the Park.
cards.source_title: Conejo Community Park — Conejo Recreation & Park District
cards.access_notes: Concert dates and any event-specific conditions vary; confirm the district’s current event information before visiting.

cards.title: Borchard Community Park — skatepark
cards.subtitle: Reino Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the districtwide skatepark during open park hours and follow posted rules; the site also has courts, fields, picnic areas, and community rooms.
cards.short_summary: A 29-acre community park whose amenities include a districtwide skatepark.
cards.evidence_claim: Borchard Community Park at 190 Reino Road includes a districtwide skatepark as well as courts, fields, picnic areas, and community rooms.
cards.source_title: Borchard Community Park — Conejo Recreation & Park District
cards.access_notes: Park open daily 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; check the district’s open-gym and skatepark information for program-specific access.

cards.title: Dos Vientos Community Park — courts and fields
cards.subtitle: Borchard Road corridor
cards.notes: Plan a daytime walk around the community park, then use its picnic areas, courts, or fields only as their availability and reservation status allow.
cards.short_summary: A 28-acre community park with fields, courts, rooms, and picnic areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Dos Vientos Community Park at 4801 Borchard Road has reservable picnic areas and rooms, fields, and sports courts for day and evening use.
cards.source_title: Dos Vientos Community Park — Conejo Recreation & Park District
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; reservations may be required for specific facilities.

cards.entity_name: Satwiwa Native American Indian Culture Center
cards.title: Satwiwa Culture Center — exhibits and programs
cards.subtitle: Lynn Road corridor
cards.notes: Visit on a weekend for the cultural exhibits and seasonal Native American programs; review the National Park Service’s current hours before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A National Park Service cultural center at the Lynn Road and Via Goleta entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Satwiwa Native American Indian Culture Center, at the Lynn Road and Via Goleta entrance in Newbury Park, offers cultural exhibits and seasonal Native American programs.
cards.source_title: Operating Hours & Seasons — Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area
cards.access_notes: Open Saturday and Sunday, 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; closed Monday–Friday and on most federal holidays.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Cal Lutheran rituals and recurring campus gatherings, from the ridge-top rocks to student-programmed seasonal events.

cards.title: Paint the CLU Rocks
cards.subtitle: Mount Clef Ridge overlooking campus
cards.notes: View the ridge landmark from campus; painting is reserved for the annual freshman and transfer-student tradition.
cards.short_summary: A long-running welcome ritual centered on the giant CLU letters above campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran says the CLU rocks have been a fixture since 1962 and that freshman and transfer students paint them every year.
cards.source_title: The ABC's of Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Observe from permitted campus areas; the official page identifies painting as an annual freshman and transfer-student activity.

cards.title: Learn the Violet and Gold Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Cal Lutheran’s school song, written in 1961
cards.notes: Read the official lyrics before a campus ceremony or reunion, and listen for the repeated violet-and-gold refrain.
cards.short_summary: The school song names Cal Lutheran, its surrounding hills, and its violet-and-gold colors.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s official glossary identifies its Alma Mater, credits Orville Dahl and Rossini/Ramsey, and dates it to 1961.
cards.source_title: The ABC's of Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: Lyrics are publicly available on the official glossary page.

cards.title: Return for the Scandinavian Festival
cards.subtitle: Annual Nordic-heritage gathering on the Cal Lutheran campus
cards.notes: Check the festival’s official schedule before going; the university describes music, dance, crafts, storytelling, and heritage activities.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus festival connecting Cal Lutheran’s Scandinavian roots with Nordic cultural programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran describes the Scandinavian Festival as an annual event celebrating the university’s Scandinavian heritage.
cards.source_title: CLU's Scandinavian Heritage
cards.access_notes: Confirm dates, admission, and activities with the festival’s current official information before attending.

cards.title: Mark the ASCLUG Fall Carnival
cards.subtitle: Kingsmen Park
cards.notes: Use the ASCLUG calendar for the current date and plan to arrive during the listed event window at Kingsmen Park.
cards.short_summary: A student-government fall gathering built around carnival games and live entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: ASCLUG lists its Fall Carnival at Kingsmen Park as a fall-semester event with carnival games and live entertainment.
cards.source_title: ASCLUG Events
cards.access_notes: The current ASCLUG calendar lists the 2026 event for October 16, 6–10 p.m.; verify future dates before attending.

cards.title: Catch Let It Snow
cards.subtitle: End-of-semester event at Kingsmen Park
cards.notes: Look to ASCLUG’s event calendar near semester’s end and use the posted time and location for the current edition.
cards.short_summary: ASCLUG’s seasonal campus celebration brings holiday programming to Kingsmen Park.
cards.evidence_claim: ASCLUG’s official events page lists Let It Snow as an end-of-semester celebration at Kingsmen Park.
cards.source_title: ASCLUG Events
cards.access_notes: The current ASCLUG calendar lists the 2026 event for December 4, 6–8 p.m.; verify future dates before attending.

cards.title: Follow Competing for the Crown
cards.subtitle: ASCLUG Programs Board event
cards.notes: Check the student-events calendar for the current format and timing; this is one of the Programs Board’s named campus events.
cards.short_summary: A named ASCLUG Programs Board gathering listed alongside Fall Carnival and Let It Snow.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s catalog names Competing for the Crown as an ASCLUG Programs Board-sponsored student event.
cards.source_title: Student Life — California Lutheran University Catalog
cards.access_notes: No current date or format was verified; consult ASCLUG’s current events calendar.

cards.title: Say Buh Bye to the Semester
cards.subtitle: ASCLUG end-of-semester gathering
cards.notes: Watch the student-events calendar late in spring and follow the official listing for the current venue and activity details.
cards.short_summary: A named Cal Lutheran send-off event for the end of the academic semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s student-life catalog identifies Buh Bye Bash among events sponsored by the Office of Student Life.
cards.source_title: Student Life — California Lutheran University Catalog
cards.access_notes: A 2026 listing placed Buh Bye Bash at Samuelson Aquatics Center; verify the current event listing before attending.

cards.entity_name: Raíces y Ritmos: Latine Heritage Fiesta
cards.title: Join Raíces y Ritmos
cards.subtitle: Annual Latine Heritage Fiesta at Kingsmen Park
cards.notes: Check the calendar around Latine Heritage Month and use the current listing for program details and attendance information.
cards.short_summary: A sixth-annual campus fiesta recognizing Latine Heritage Month through community, culture, music, and connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s events calendar calls Raíces y Ritmos its sixth annual Latine Heritage Fiesta and says it honors Latine Heritage Month.
cards.source_title: The Hub — Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, Justice and Belonging
cards.access_notes: The current calendar lists a September 25, 2026 event at Kingsmen Park; verify future dates before attending.

cards.title: See Dragged Out
cards.subtitle: CCEI’s annual celebration of the art of drag
cards.notes: Consult the CCEI calendar for the current date, venue, and participation details before making plans for this performance event.
cards.short_summary: An annual CCEI event celebrating drag performance and self-expression on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s events calendar describes Dragged Out as the CCEI’s annual celebration of the art of drag.
cards.source_title: The Hub — Student Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: The current calendar lists a 2026 event at Lundring Events Center; verify future dates and access information before attending.

cards.title: Trace the Choir’s Annual Tour
cards.subtitle: A tradition first recorded in 1962
cards.notes: Look for current choir announcements or concert listings; the university history records the first annual tour with 50 student singers.
cards.short_summary: A music tradition whose first annual tour is documented in Cal Lutheran’s institutional history.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Lutheran’s history states that its Choir began its first annual tour in April 1962 with 50 students.
cards.source_title: History of Cal Lutheran
cards.access_notes: The history page documents the tradition’s 1962 beginning; no current tour schedule was verified.
